headline: A missing object is `objectstore/not-found` on every backend
summary: `b.storage.exists` returns `false` when the backend reports `objectstore/not-found` and propagates anything else, so a transient outage is never read as absence. Only the local and S3 backends produced that code: on Azure Blob and GCS a missing key surfaced as a raw HTTP failure, so `exists` threw where it documents `false`. Every backend now reports a missing key the same way.

items.title: `b.storage.exists` threw on Azure Blob and GCS instead of returning `false`
items.body:
`exists` calls the backend's `head` and returns `false` on `objectstore/not-found`. The local and S3/sigv4 backends mapped a missing key to that code; Azure Blob and GCS re-threw the transport's own error, carrying `statusCode: 404`. An operator gating a downstream write on `exists` got an exception rather than a boolean, on two of the four shipped backends.

A 404 on a `get`, `getResponse` or `head` is now `objectstore/not-found` on every HTTP backend — S3/sigv4, Azure Blob, GCS and http-put — mapped in one place rather than in each of them. The mapped error still carries `statusCode: 404`, so a caller that reads the status instead of the code is unaffected. Nothing else is remapped: any other status propagates exactly as before, which is what keeps a 503 from being read as absence.

On the HTTP backends the code means "the object endpoint answered 404". A provider returns that for a missing container or bucket as well, and a HEAD carries no body while the error carries no response headers, so the two are not distinguishable at this layer. `b.storage.exists` returning `false` therefore means the object is not readable at that path rather than that the store is healthy and the object absent; its documentation now says so. That was already the behaviour on S3/sigv4 before this release, and the other backends now match it.

The same gap was present on the S3/sigv4 `get` path, where only `head` had ever mapped it.

items.title: An ICAP error verdict from `b.mail.scan` now names its error
items.body: `errorCode` and `errorMessage` were added to clamav-instream error verdicts in 0.19.6, and an ICAP error verdict carried neither, so a caller handling `verdict: "error"` had to know which backend answered before it could find out what went wrong. An ICAP response whose status is neither 200 nor 204 now reports `mail-scan/icap-status` with the status line, and still carries the parsed `icapResponse` alongside it. A clean or infected verdict carries no error fields, as before.

items.title: Vendored `@blamejs/pki` moves to 0.6.55
items.body: `lib/vendor/blamejs-pki.cjs` carries 0.6.55, refreshed through `scripts/vendor-update.sh`, with the `MANIFEST.json` SHA-256 hashes regenerated alongside it. The certificate, PKI and WebAuthn paths that read it are unchanged here.

items.title: Seventeen comments in the shipped source were half-sentences
items.body: The 0.19.0 comment sweep removed lines from multi-line comment blocks and, where it removed only part of one, left the remainder behind. Seventeen blocks in `lib/` ended mid-sentence or opened mid-clause. `lib/` ships in the package, so these were visible to anyone reading the installed source. Each is now a complete statement or is gone.
